transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Southport Head of AI), Sofia Martinez (Cloud Architect), Jamal Rivers (Procurement)

Summary: quick renewal/expansion sync focused on adding capacity (more reserved GPU pools), spinning up EU region nodes, and aligning contract extension timing. Security/compliance and cost per token tradeoffs discussed. Action items and next steps agreed at the end.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Marcus, Sofia, Jamal, great to see you. Quick intro, I'm Avery, AE on the account, and Priya's our SE who will cover the bench—benchmarks and capacity details.
[00:18] Marcus Lee: Hey, thanks. Appreciate it. We just wanted to get alignment on renewal timeline and the extra capacity ask we raised last week.
[00:25] Priya Rao: Yeah, hi all. Quick agenda, we'll run through current usage, proposed dedicated capacity tiers, EU region setup, and then procurement/contract timing.
[00:35] Sofia Martinez: Also SOC two questions—sorry SOC two—yeah, and some KMS/HSM details for the EU region.
[00:42] Jamal Rivers: And procurement just needs rough numbers for OPEX vs commit.

[01:10] Avery Chen: Cool. So current state — you're on the hosted plan with a small reserved commitment (we pulled the usage report), average p95 latency is ~220ms for your typical 512 token responses, monthly tokens around 120M, with burst events that spike CPU/GPU use. Your renewal is Feb 1, 2027, and you've flagged wanting more predictable throughput for Q2. Does that align with how you see it?
[01:35] Marcus Lee: Yep, that matches. Also, we're increasing the chat assistants across more products and expect a 2.5x token growth by May. So we want to reserve capacity and also add EU region to reduce latency for EU customers.
[01:48] Priya Rao: That makes sense. Two levers: add dedicated pools (reserved GPUs) in NA and EU, and we can increase burst capacity for peaks. Dedicated pools give you predictable throughput and improved cold-start characteristics. There's also quantization profiles to reduce cost per token but with slight quality tradeoffs.
[02:10] Sofia Martinez: For EU, do you support private VPC connections from our GCP tenant? We need traffic to stay regionally bound for compliance.
[02:20] Priya Rao: Yes, Redwood Private supports VPC peering and on-prem options; for hosted/dedicated we offer customer VPC peering and private link into EU region. There was a small note—sometimes the peering setup can change with cloud provider VLAN mappings, so we'd work through the network runbook.
[02:35] Marcus Lee: Good. On security we need SOC2 Type II, ISO, and audit logs retention for 2 years.
[02:42] Avery Chen: We can provide SOC 2 and ISO docs. Our audit log retention add-on can be extended to 24 months; I'll include that in the pricing.

[03:10] Jamal Rivers: Pricing—so how much does each dedicated pool cost and what's the delta vs hosted? We need ballpark now to prep the budget.
[03:20] Priya Rao: Rough numbers: a small dedicated pool (2x A100-class equivalent) is about $Xk/month, medium (4x) $Yk/month, and large (8x) $Zk/month — I'll put exact numbers in the sheet. Usually teams pair a medium pool with intelligent batching + KV cache to cut unit costs by ~30%.
[03:40] Marcus Lee: Can you also show the model fallbacks if capacity is constrained? We have strict Uptime SLOs for payments and we need graceful degradation.
[03:50] Priya Rao: Absolutely—smart routing can route to lower-cost model variants or other regions automatically. We can configure canary failovers and keep strict latency SLOs on key routes.

[04:20] Avery Chen: One nuance—if you want EU region dedicated pools, there's usually a one-time onboarding for regional infra and estimated 3–4 week lead time. That affects start date if you want go-live by April.
[04:32] Sofia Martinez: 3–4 weeks is fine if we sign in January. Is there a way to pre-book slots? Our traffic spike in March is unavoidable.
[04:40] Priya Rao: We do capacity reservations for Dedicated — committing earlier gives higher priority for slot allocation. I'll mark that in the proposal.

[05:05] Marcus Lee: On benchmarking — can Redwood run a latency/cost benchmark with our sample workload in EU? We want real numbers to show to engineering and procurement.
[05:15] Priya Rao: Yes, we can run a benchmark. We'll need a sample prompt set, expected concurrency, and tokens per call. If you can provide that by Monday, we can run it on a test EU pool and share raw metrics.
[05:28] Marcus Lee: We'll send that. Expect to include load pattern during peak hour.

[06:00] Jamal Rivers: Contract amendments—we'd like an option to add capacity mid-term without re-signing the whole contract. Is that supported?
[06:08] Avery Chen: Yes, we have a contract amendment template for capacity add-ons; you can purchase an add-on and it will prorate. For a longer commitment extension (12 vs 24 months) we can offer a discount. I'll include both options in the pricing sheet.
[06:25] Jamal Rivers: For procurement, we might need a 90-day cancellation right on the dedicated capacity for the first quarter — is that negotiable?
[06:33] Avery Chen: We can discuss that with legal — typical reserved contracts have a notice period, but for strategic customers we can add flexibility in the amendment. I'll flag legal involvement.

[07:10] Sofia Martinez: A couple of technical details: does the EU deployment use the same model catalog? We need Redwood-verified model profiles for the smaller quantized variants.
[07:18] Priya Rao: Yes, same catalog. We can pin model versions per region and per pool. The Redwood-verified profiles include quantization recommendations and perf numbers; note that quantized models sometimes show minor regen differences — we recommend running your evals against golden prompts.
[07:35] Marcus Lee: Can we keep KV cache across regions or is it regional? We want to avoid cache misses when routing between NA and EU during failover.
[07:44] Priya Rao: KV cache is regional by default to meet data residency; cross-region cache replication is possible but has latency and compliance tradeoffs. For critical routes we usually keep session pinning to a region and use fallback only for non-cached calls.

[08:10] Avery Chen: Quick note on metrics: we'll provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route SLO dashboards in the Console. You can share dashboard access for your devs.
[08:20] Marcus Lee: Perfect. Also put together a short one-pager that shows cost tradeoffs (dedicated vs hosted + quantization) because our CFO wants a succinct slide.
[08:29] Avery Chen: Will do. I'll attach a simple cost comparison and the commitment discount table.

[09:00] Priya Rao: One small transcription quirk — sometimes model names get transposed in the notes, e.g., 'Redwood Dedicated' might show up as 'Redwood dedicate' in some logs, so ignore small typos.
[09:12] Jamal Rivers: (laughs) noted.

[09:40] Marcus Lee: On compliance docs, we'll need key management details — KMS integration, whether keys are customer-managed, HSM options for EU.
[09:50] Priya Rao: We support KMS integrations with customer-managed keys and HSM-backed keystores for Private deployments. For hosted/dedicated, we provide envelope encryption with customer KMS and options to use our HSM partners; I'll include the KMS integration guide link in the docs.

[10:20] Avery Chen: Okay let's recap — key asks: 1) pricing + amendment with dedicated tiers and 24-month audit logs; 2) EU dedicated pool onboarding timing and seat reservations; 3) benchmark run in EU with Marcus's prompt set; 4) list of compliance docs (SOC2, ISO, KMS/HSM info). We'll deliver those.
[10:40] Marcus Lee: Yep, and procurement will review the amendment. If the numbers look good we can target a Jan signature and Feb/Mar onboarding for NA; EU go-live end of March/early April if benchmarks clear.

[11:05] Jamal Rivers: Sounds good. Anything else?
[11:10] Avery Chen: I think that's it. I'll follow up with the pricing sheet and the contract amendment template after this call. Priya will reach out to set up the benchmark and share a runbook for network peering.
[11:25] Marcus Lee: Thanks everyone.
[11:28] Sofia Martinez: Thanks.
[11:30] End of call.

Notes: transcript includes natural speech patterns, a few small mis-transcriptions, and short references to docs: pricing sheet link (internal): https://redwood.example.com/pricing/southport, KMS integration guide: https://redwood.example.com/docs/kms, onboarding runbook: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/eu-onboard.
